messages:
anya: heads-up, ran a quick smoke of 'samplecraft' speculative decode on llama4t-13b-q4 and saw ~1.8x token/s improvement but a small quality wobble on long-form.
matt: nice. what's the config? seed, prefix length, speculative policy?
anya: short summary \n```\nmodel: llama4t-13b-q4\nquant: q4_k_mixed\nbatch: 8\nshort_prefix: 32\nspeculative_stage: 1\nfallback_prob: 0.06\nseed: 42\n```\nused our standard rerank holdout (500 prompts, mixed long/short).
kevin: did you include kv-cache warmup? that can explain longform regressions.
anya: yes; warmup=128 tokens. the regressions look like hallucinated facts at paragraph boundaries, not just token-fluency.
samira: can you dump diffs for the worst 20 examples? also run deterministic sampling (top_k=1) to isolate noise.
anya: uploading diffs now (link) — quick highlights: 12/20 show extra invented clause, 5/20 are cutoff truncation earlier than baseline.
jordan: curious if quantization plays a role — q4 sometimes shifts logits in low-prob tails, speculative decoding might amplify that.
matt: let's run two controls: (A) same decode but fp16 (no quant) (B) q4 + no speculative. compare per-example BLEU/ROUGE and our human-flip metric.
kevin: add per-token perplexity delta and entropic score (avg top-10 entropy). if entropy drops below threshold after speculative step, that's a red flag.
anya: agreed. I'm kicking off 3 jobs now. ETA ~25m. tagging @eng-sre if infra spikes.
ops-bot: deploy-burst started for job ids [sc-1729901234-a, sc-1729901234-b, sc-1729901234-c] — expected runtime 30m.
samira: for eval methodology: use paired bootstrap for significance, and compute fraction of prompts with harmful factual flips. log tokens where KV cache index changed.
jordan: also test with longer short_prefix variants (64,128) — maybe the early-shot speculative step is too short for some long contexts.
anya: good call. adding (short_prefix=64) to run c.
matt: if quality holds for fp16 but not q4, we should try q4+PTQ-refine (small calibration set) before ruling out speculative technique.
kevin: note: if fallback_prob > 0.05 we reduce speed gains; might tune adaptively based on entropy window.
anya: will share results in this thread. for now labeling this 'mini-smoke/samplecraft' — keep eyes open for any infra errors.
ops-bot: job sc-1729901234-a completed (fp16-control) — 27m. artifacts: s3://redwood-sandbox/sc/1729901234/a
anya: received. starting quick diff analysis.
matt: thanks. when diff summary is up let's decide whether to proceed to a small human eval.
anya: diff summary: fp16 baseline vs samplecraft-q4: 1.9x speed, 0.7% drop in paired accept rate (p=0.02), 0.4 BLEU avg drop concentrated in long prompts. uploading csv.
samira: 0.7% seems borderline but p=0.02 is noteworthy. propose 200 human judgments focusing on factuality and coherence.
jordan: if we can mitigate via longer prefix or adaptive fallback, we keep win. otherwise it's risky for production.
anya: creating a small A/B job for 200 human labels. will include variants: q4+pref64+adapt-fallback, q4+ptq-refine, and fp16 baseline.
matt: perfect. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
_meta: generated as a single-thread slack dump; messages are chronological and prefixed by sender display names
